 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.

That, on 14.02.2023 at about 6.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a Private bus bearing registration No.KA-22/B-3949, when the bus reached near Bypanahalli bus stand, Bhaktharahalli Post, Sasalu Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, the driver stopped the bus to get down the passengers, when the petitioner was getting down from the bus, at that time the driver of said bus without observing the passengers,
suddenly moved the same, as a result of which, the petitioner was pulled on the earth and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to We-Care Multi Speciality Hospital, Doddaballapura for first aid, thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient for a day, then he was shifted to BGS hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for a day and also took treatment as out patient and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.

4. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 63 years, doing coolie and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Private bus bearing registration No.KA-22/B-3949.

In this regard, case was registered against driver of said vehicle by the jurisdictional Doddabelavangala Singrappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144105763/
2 Police in Crime No.50/2023.

sentences.text: As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 & 3 have not appeared before the court, remained absent, hence they were placed exparte.

7. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Private bus bearing registration No.KA-22/B- 3949 and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contention of the respondent No.1 that alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident which is result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Private Bus bearing registration No.KA-22-B-3949?
2. Whether respondent No.1 proves that the passenger bus bearing registration No.KA-22-B-3949 was not involved in the accident?
3. Whether respondent No.1 proves that respondent No.2 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy?
4. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
5.
What order
or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, petitioner has placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
10.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW1 and got marked the documents on his behalf as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
11.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

sentences.text:
My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the Negative Issue No.3: In the Negative Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.5: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1 & ISSUE No.2:-
13.These issues are interlinked with each other, in order to avoid repetition of facts these issues are taken together for common discussion.
14.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Private bus bearing registration No.KA-22/B-3949 the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

15. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 & 3 being the owners of the offending vehicle placed exparte.
In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case got examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to P7.
Ex. P1-
true copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2- true copy of the first information statement given by one Revanna, Ex.P3 & Ex.P4 - true copies of Spot mahazar, Ex

.P5- true copy of the wound certificate,
Ex.P6- true copy of IMV report & Ex
.P7- true copy of charge sheet in Crime No.50/2023 of Dodda Belavangala Police Station.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by one Revanna, son of the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Dodda Belavangala Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
18.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 examined its Administrative Officer as RW1.

He has deposed in his evidence that as per Ex.P5, Ex.P8 and Ex.P9 pertaining to the petitioner Sinagarappa has taken treatment 14.2.2023 with the history of RTA-fall from moving bus on 14.2.2025 around 6.30 p.m. near Bigppanahalli bus stop and sustained head injuries, it clearly shows that the injured has sustained injuries by his own negligence.
Further contended that there was delay in lodging complaint after lapse of 17 days.
No valid reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.
So the petitioner was falsely implicated the insured vehicle.

sentences.text: On going through the recitals of the complaint and the reasons given by the complainant about the delay in giving first information is concerned one can say that, if a person severely injured in the accident, one cannot expect immediate complaint about the accident instead of providing treatment.

Delay in giving first information always cannot be looked in a suspicious manner, the said point of delay is to be considered by looking into the each facts and circumstances and also the reasons set out in the complaint, on the point of delay.
As already discussed supra, the complainant who is none other than the son of the petitioner gave clear explanation in the complaint, on the point of delay.
Hence, I am of the view that the delay in giving first information about the accident in the case on hand is not fatal.
Hence, it is necessary to note down the decision reported in (2011) 4 SCC Page 693, between, Ravi V/S. Badrinarayan.

20. Apart from this it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.1 has not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to prove that as on the date of accident the petitioner himself fall from the bus and not on the fault of the driver of the bus.

21. PW1 was subjected to cross-examination at length, but nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
22. In the light of the evidence placed on record, the respondent No.1 has utterly failed to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement by placing acceptable evidence on record.

Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence to prove the above issue to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the private bus bearing registration No.KA-22-B-3949.

Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative and the issue No.2 is in the Negative.

ISSUE No.3;
23.
This issue is with respect to the violation of fundamental conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.1 has stated that the driver of the Private bus bearing No.KA-22-B-3949 had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Hence, respondent No.3 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy.
Though he has examined officer of the company, but his evidence will not much help to prove its contention.
He has placed authorisation letter, policy copy and letter sent to respondent No.3.
These documents are not sufficient to prove his defence.

Hence,
it is clear that the respondent No.1 has failed to prove that the respondent No.3 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy.
Hence, I answer the issue No.3 in the Negative.

ISSUE No.4:
24.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Fracture of left parietal bone extended to right parietal bone 2) Fracture of right temporal bone 3) Acute subarachoinoid hemorrhage in left frontal lobe 4) Right sided ear bleed Acute subdural hematoma with active bleeding along with left frontal lobe.
27.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Except production of wound certificate, case referral record, CT scan the petitioner has not produced discharge summary to show that how many days he took the treatment as an inpatient.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:

sentences.text: PW1 has stated that, he was doing agriculture and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
There is no iota of documents to show that the petitioner was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Hence, it is apt to be considered notional income.
The petitioenr has not placed discharge summary to show that how many days he took the treatment as inpatient.
Anyhow, by considering the nature of the injuries definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months.
by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.32,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
29.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.20,502/- as per Ex.P11.
In the cross- examination suggested that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,502/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
30.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records the petitioner has taken treatment for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food,
nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
31.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

Except the production of medical documents and averments made in the main petition as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor, in order to prove the disability sustained by him, due to the accidental injuries in order to know, whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner will effect to his future and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort to the petitioner to do his routine work as well as his work for his avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner.
Further the petitioner has continued his service as usual.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future income due to want of evidence on record.

Loss of amenities;
32.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to Acute subdural hematoma with active bleeding along with left frontal convexity, acute subrachnoid contusion in left frontal lobe, right side ear bleaded.
Fracture of left parietal bone with extension to right parietal bone, fracture of right temporal bone.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a Singrappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144105763/
7 mason.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities.
33. In connection with the future medication, the petitioner has not placed any documents for consideration.
Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation of under the head of future medical expenses.

34. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 40,000-00
2.Loss of income during Rs. 32,000-00 laid-up period and rest period
3. Medical expenses Rs. 20,502-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income NIL due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 10,000-00 7.
Future medication NIL Total Rs.1,12,502-00 35

. As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner u/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,12,502/- (Rupees one lakh twelve thousand five hundred and two only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the amount is very meager, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 8th day of May 2025).
